To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stability of steady shear-band solutions in an elastoplasticty model for granular flows depends on a dimensionless number that is proportional to the inverse ratio of the mesh to macroscopic length scales.

the introduction of discreteness into an otherwise continuum model for granular material flow results in bounded solutions, and that the presence of an elastic shear modulus stabilizes the flow, whereas the absence of elasticity destabilizes it.

the introduction of discreteness into a continuum model for granular shear flow leads to stable steady-state solutions, but that these lose stability through a bifurcation to time-periodic solutions as the elastic modulus decreases below a critical threshold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of discretness in a continuum model of granular flow, with particular attention given to the role of elastic shear modulus.
the role of discretness in the stability of shear bands in continuum models of granular flow.
the effect of discreteness on the stability and bifurcation of solutions to continuum equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the model with discreteness predicts that shear bands are stable in the macroscopic limit, but that the stability of shear bands is lost when ℰ becomes smaller than a threshold value proportional to the ratio between the macroscopic length-scale and the mesh size.
the stability of shear bands in a discrete elastoplasticity continuum model for granular flows is governed by the interplay of discreteness and non-linearity.
discreteness is responsible for stability of steady states and that the loss of stability is caused by a combination of discreteness and non-linearity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
discreteness is a key ingredient in stabilizing granular flow.
discreteness is crucial in stabilizing the system and that the bifurcation is of the Hopf type.

the discrete model has the following properties: (i) bounded solutions for all times, (ii) stability of the steady-state solutions for large and moderate ℰ, and (iii) instability of the steady-state solution for small ℰ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
discreteness, in the form of finite differences, can stabilize the system of continuum equations and give rise to a rich variety of solutions.
the stability properties of a continuum model can change drastically upon discretization, even if the mesh is sufficiently fine.
, for a continuum elastoplastic model of granular flow, discreteness can have a significant effect on stability.
